summary: The deterministic review-escalation policy as an explicit, machine-diffable CONTRACT (#2566, first concrete instance of spec-based programming #2564, under #2563 Fork 1). It declares — as DATA, not code — the three policy VALUES that used to live only as literals inside the derivation code: the rubric thresholds, the escalation-reason vocabulary with each reason's family + clearance, and the strictest-wins disposition decision table. The DERIVATION LOGIC (scoreEscalation, deriveReviewDisposition) stays in code and is proven to realize this table by the conformance suite (review-policy.conformance.test.mjs). Because every VALUE lives here and nowhere else, 'did the policy change?' collapses to 'did this file change?' — a deterministic yes/no. A diff to this file trips the trust-chain policy-tier path test and forces review:human; an implementation change that keeps the conformance suite green is agent-clearable (a 1-char threshold flip is a SPEC change here → human; a behaviour-preserving refactor of the branches is IMPL → agent). Per #2564 a spec is a schema skeleton + a first-class prose layer in one artifact: the machine-checkable shape is the fields below, the contract's MEANING is the 'description' prose on each entry. An entry may also declare itself NOT YET IMPLEMENTED via the `todo` + `owedTo` marker — see the `todoMarker` block below for what that costs and what the gate does about it.

thresholds.description: The rubric tuning knobs — loose to start, tightened from data. These are the ONLY home for the numbers; the code (scripts/lib/review-escalation.mjs DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS) imports them from here, so flipping one is necessarily a diff to THIS file → a human-gated spec change.

diffLines.description: A PR changing at least this many total lines escalates on size alone. Size is a care-level signal (raises the convergence loop's scrutiny), not a hard block (#2563).

todoMarker.description: The NOT-YET-IMPLEMENTED marker — how a contract entry declares itself DECLARED-BUT-UNBUILT, and the honest price of doing so. WHY IT EXISTS: #2839 relaxed the conformance suite's reason-token pin from set EQUALITY to directional CONTAINMENT (code may never outrun the spec; the spec MAY outrun the code) so a principle PR can land ahead of its impl PR. That relaxation made a THIRD state legal — declared in the contract, absent from the code, and UNMARKED — and it passed the suite whose entire job is to be the deterministic backstop. Worse than invisible: the only assertion it tripped was the decorated-fixture-map pin, whose message tells the author to add a decorated fixture, after which the phantom entry is fully green. A `todo` marker turns that third state from an accident into a DECLARATION. HOW TO MARK AN ENTRY: add `"todo": true` and pair it with `"owedTo": "<backlog item>"` naming the OPEN item that will build it (an `NNN` number or an `xNNNNNN` hash; a leading `#` is tolerated). The two fields are inseparable in BOTH directions — `todo` without `owedTo` is a free pass and is refused at load; `owedTo` without `todo` claims an implemented entry is owed something and is refused too. It is the same FAMILY of honest escape the invariant catalogue already carries — `status: "judgment-only"`, 6 entries in we:scripts/lib/invariant-catalogue.json — but deliberately STRONGER: that escape records only that a guarantee is unenforced, and has no field naming who owes the work, so nothing goes stale when the work lands. Adding an owing item to that catalogue is what #2844 PROPOSES; #2844 is still `status: open` and unbuilt, so this marker is not modelled on it and does not wait for it. The principle both share: a guarantee the repo has RULED but not yet BUILT does not get to read as built. WHAT THE GATE ENFORCES, and the half `test.todo` does not: the conformance suite pins (contract entries MINUS todo entries) EXACTLY equal to the code's vocabulary, in both directions. Absent-and-unmarked fails (the hole above). And a STALE marker — an entry still marked `todo` that the code has since IMPLEMENTED — fails too, which `test.todo` itself never catches: it reports a todo that passes as a note, never as a defect, so a marker outlives its work indefinitely. Here the marker must be REMOVED in the same PR that lands the impl, or the suite is red. TREAT IT AS DEBT, NOT A DIALECT: a `todo` entry is inert — it is excluded from every derived constant the impl imports, so it can never reach runtime classification, and a decorated-fixture pin ignores it (there is no emitted string to fix). It changes NO behaviour; it only reserves the vocabulary and names the debt.

reasons.description: The diff edits the DECLARATIVE LEASH of the auto-review trust chain — the encoded policy itself: this contract, the gate-config roster, and the invariant / conformance suites (POLICY_SPEC_BASENAMES, gate-config.mjs). Those files ARE the policy, so there is no behaviour-preserving edit to them and 'did the spec change?' is exactly 'did this file change?' — a human is essential (#2285, narrowed to the leash by #2771/#2785). Fires at classification time (before any review deadlock), so the panel may CONVERGE an advisory fix — but it never auto-lands. NOTE the narrowing kept this token's NAME and its human clearance unchanged on purpose: a PR already parked with a `gate-self` reason before #2785 landed keeps its human gate, and only the newly-split `gate-derivation` token below is agent-clearable.

The diff edits policy-tier DERIVATION CODE — the code that derives the gate from the declarative leash (the rubric review-escalation.mjs, the disposition router review-core.mjs, the contract loader review-policy.mjs, the two land seams). Ratified agent-clearable by #2771 Fork A (`#review-human-declarative-leash-only`): an independent, fresh-context committee that took no part in authoring the diff is sufficient independence for the CODE, PROVIDED the leash it implements stays human-gated (the `gate-self` token above) and the conformance suite stays green. The suite is the deterministic backstop — any change that alters the gate's BEHAVIOUR reddens conformance, which forces a contract diff, which is human-gated. So: escalates and runs the full panel, and a converged verdict lands; non-convergence still hands to a human.

The diff edits the statute layer (platform-decisions.md / any statute doc) — a governance rule a human must ratify (#2412). Same disposition as gate-self: converge an advisory fix, never auto-land. UNCHANGED by the #2771/#2785 narrowing: every statute edit still fires this token and still forces a human.

The diff changes what an automated actor may do: a `permissions:` line or scope grant in .github/workflows/*, a sandbox grant (Codex writable roots, --add-dir, sandbox_mode, ...), or branch-protection-adjacent config (CODEOWNERS, rulesets, the required-checks roster). Operator decision 2026-10-08, after PR #4318 widened a workflow token to contents: write and merged on the automatic accept. Same disposition as gate-self: converge an advisory fix, never auto-land; the drain also refuses a bare review:accepted without a recorded human clearance bound to the live head (decideReviewGate).

The diff touches a high-blast-radius surface (scripts, the agent-behaviour trees — skills and agent memory, in BOTH their .claude/ link spelling and their skills-src/ + agent-memory-src/ source spelling, #2909 — hooks, CI, the statute layer, standards defs) OR the engine tier of the trust chain (the lander). Escalation-worthy — a bad merge here is costlier than a leaf edit — but agent-reviewable: a converged verdict lands (#2445 two-tier flip). The statute layer is the exception that is ALSO human-gated: it is blast-radius here and separately carries the `statute` token's human clearance.
Total changed lines reached thresholds.diffLines. A care-level signal, agent-clearable on a converged verdict.

The lane's pre-PR review dismissed one or more findings — the strongest scored signal (it targets author anchoring: the lane judged its own reviewer's findings away). Agent-clearable on a converged verdict.
An impl+WE couple spanning more than one repo — a coordinated multi-repo change. Agent-clearable on a converged verdict.
The panel-editor negotiation loop already ran and could not agree within its round cap. Re-converging just repeats the deadlock, so this hands straight to a human — no further convergence.
The review panel surfaced a genuine mutually-exclusive tradeoff between mandatory lenses (e.g. security wants X, simplicity wants not-X) — human judgment by definition. Hands straight to a human.

disposition.description: The strictest-reason-wins decision table deriveReviewDisposition realizes: given the reason(s) a PR escalated for, what does a review surface DO about it — { mode: converge | human, autoLand }. Rules are evaluated in order (strictest first); the FIRST rule whose predicate matches ANY of the PR's reasons wins. 'match' is a predicate over a reason's declared family/clearance above. autoLand=false is the single enforcement point for the #2285 conflict-of-interest invariant: a human gates the merge regardless of how clean the findings look.

precedence.description: Any deadlock reason: the convergence loop already failed, so a human decides — no (re-)convergence. Evaluated first, so a deadlock reason beats every sensitivity reason in the same set.

A human-clearance SENSITIVITY reason (gate-self or statute — deadlock is already caught above): converge an ADVISORY fix, but a human must still clear the merge. The #2445 two-tier flip keeps ONLY these two sensitivity classes human; the lander (engine tier) falls through to the next rule, and since #2771/#2785 so does `gate-derivation` (policy-tier code that is not the leash).
Any other sensitivity reason: agent-reviewable — a converged verdict lands. This is the catch-all for the remaining scored signals.

careJury.description: The care→jury table (#2633, foundation slice of the jury cluster #2636). For each advisory care band (the CARE_LEVELS enum none/low/elevated/high, single-sourced in review-escalation.mjs) this declares — as DATA — WHICH lenses fan out, HOW MANY jurors per lens, the per-band roundCap (the max editor↔reviewer round-trips that band runs before a deadlock hands to a human), and the OPTIONAL validation methods each lens may pull in. It single-sources the bands hardcoded today in jury-core.mjs panelRigorForCareLevel (roundCap here is that function's per-band `rounds`): the conformance suite pins the two equal, so a re-tune becomes one human-gated edit to THIS file, not scattered constants. FORWARD-FIT NOW FILLED IN (#2651, ratified record 273a2dbd, FF3): the disposition-config knobs the #2633 shape reserved room for are now concrete under `disposition` below — per-lens/juror weights, a dissent-tolerance threshold, and a resolutionMode (accept-best ↔ present-unless-all-agree), each overridable per care band and per decision. #2633 deliberately left every band an OPEN object and the shape validator tolerant of unknown keys, so #2651 adds these as PURELY ADDITIVE keys — an edit, never a migration; no existing band value changed. This is the CONFIG half only: the disposition JUDGE that reads it is #2652, not built here. Aggregation stays diversity-selection (strictest-wins, never a vote — #2567); resolutionMode tunes accept-best vs present-unless-all-agree WITHIN that, it never reintroduces majority voting.

disposition.description: Disposition-config knobs (#2651, ratified record 273a2dbd, FF3). These tune HOW the jury's many verdicts reduce to one fork outcome — always WITHIN diversity-selection (strictest juror wins, never a majority vote — #2567): weights say which lens counts more, the dissent threshold says how much weighted disagreement a fork tolerates before it ESCALATES instead of auto-resolving, and resolutionMode picks accept-best vs present-unless-all-agree. Each value here is the GLOBAL default. A care band may narrow it via an optional per-band `disposition` key (bands[name].disposition), and a single review subject may narrow it further via a per-decision override whose allowed keys are fixed by `override.overridableKeys`. The stateless roster recompute (F3) reads this by merging decision-override > band-override > global default (resolveDispositionConfig in review-policy.mjs). CONFIG only — the judge that consumes it is #2652.

lensWeights.description: Per-lens weight — how much a lens's verdict counts when the fork's verdicts reduce. Default 1 (equal weight); a lens absent from `values` is weight 1. A per-JUROR weight derives from its lens (jurors of the same lens share that lens's weight). Weights bias the dissent/tie accounting only; they NEVER convert diversity-selection into a majority vote (#2567). Global default is equal weight (empty map) — loose to start, tuned from data.

dissentThreshold.description: Dissent-tolerance — the fraction (0..1) of WEIGHTED juror disagreement a fork tolerates before it ESCALATES to a human rather than auto-resolving. 0 = any dissent escalates (weighted unanimity required to auto-resolve); 1 = dissent alone never escalates. A care-level signal like thresholds.diffLines: loose to start (0), tightened from data. The ONLY home for this number.

resolutionMode.description: How a fork's weighted verdicts reduce to one outcome. 'accept-best' takes the strictest single verdict and auto-resolves (diversity-selection to a decision); 'present-unless-all-agree' surfaces the fork to a human UNLESS every weighted juror agrees. The conservative default 'present-unless-all-agree' preserves #2576's the-human-disposes stance until the disposition judge (#2652) is ratified to relax it.

landMode.description: The auto-land seam's operating mode (#2675) — the ONE switch that gates whether a clean auto-dispose actually WRITES review:accepted (so the drain merges it) or merely OBSERVES what it would do. 'shadow' (the default): the seam LOGS its intended disposition for a clean auto-dispose but applies NO label and merges nothing — a human still clears the PR, for a confidence-building period. 'enforce': a clean auto-dispose writes review:accepted via decideSetLabel (INVARIANT 2 inherited unbypassed) and the drain lands it with no human in the loop. The default is SHADOW by ratified ruling (operator 2026-07-26): flipping to 'enforce' is a SEPARATE one-line ruling later, made only after shadow-mode logs build confidence. GLOBAL-only — this is a system-wide operating stance, NOT a per-band or per-decision knob, so it is absent from override.overridableKeys. Safety rails hold in BOTH modes: a red-judge-refuted or gate-self PR is never auto-landed, and any seam error fails closed to no auto-action.

override.description: The per-decision override CONTRACT — knob (4). A single review subject may override any of the three disposition knobs at runtime; this declares the ALLOW-LIST of keys an override may set, and nothing else. A decision is not known at authoring time, so the contract fixes only the SHAPE + allow-list, never the per-subject values — those arrive at runtime and the resolver merges them ahead of the band and global defaults (decision > band > global). An override naming a key outside this list is rejected.

rosterTimingMode.description: Knob #4 — WHEN the jury roster is chosen relative to the run. 'up-front' (today's behavior) picks the whole roster before any juror runs; the reserved alternative 'incremental' would add jurors as care escalates mid-run. One human-gated setting; a per-decision override may narrow it later.

none.description: The PR did not escalate — no panel, nothing to review. Zero jurors, zero rounds.

low.description: The baseline panel a routine spot-check earns — the full lens set, one juror each, a single editor↔reviewer round.

elevated.description: A system-machinery / dismissed-finding change earns a second negotiation round; still one juror per lens over the full set.

high.description: Maximum scrutiny (a gate-self/statute change, or several stacked scored signals) — three rounds and TWO jurors per lens, the diverse jury against shared blind spots.
